title: Ghana Revenue Authority launches Publican AI trade analytics, which may have recovered GH¢15 million
summary: GRA's Publican AI customs analytics, supplied by an unnamed Cyprus-based firm, rolled out from 1 February 2026 at Tema Port; the OECD AI Incidents Monitor summary says GH¢15 million was recovered, ...
account: The OECD AI Incidents Monitor entry dated 16 January 2026 summarizes Ghanaian reports that the Ghana Revenue Authority launched Publican AI. That is a trade data analytics platform to identify customs fraud, undervaluation and falsified import documentation. The entry states that the system has already recovered GH¢15 million from fraudulent importers. Its source is a GhanaWeb story titled “Government recovers GH¢15 million through new trade data system”. The entry is classified as an AI Incident with the harm type economic harm to property interests. The Ghanaian Times (Kingsley Asare, 19 January 2026) reported remarks by Commissioner-General Dr Anthony Sarpong. He said that the Publican AI system would give 100 percent coverage of assessment. He said that assessments could be completed within five minutes instead of about two hours. He said that pilots showed 40–45% revenue gains. He said that rollout would begin at Tema Port on 1 February 2026. That article cites no realized recovery. The vendor is described only as a Cyprus-based firm.
purpose: Identify customs fraud, undervaluation and falsified import documentation and give full coverage of customs assessment.
developer: A Cyprus-based firm, unnamed in the read article
taxonomy_note: Tax yield is read as the authority's revenue; Trustible's description is written for product sales.

ratings.reason: The recovery figure is a secondary summary and the revenue gain is a projection. No verified outcome for the GRA is documented.
Public revenue effects are projected, not observed, in the sources.

ai_role.statement: Neither source describes how the analytics identify undervaluation or what share of the claimed recovery the system produced. The system is vendor-built and deployed by the GRA.

headline: GRA's Publican AI may have recovered GH¢15 million

comparator.against: manual assessment and classification of goods by customs officers
comparator.before: could take up to two hours after importers submitted their documentation
comparator.after: assessments could be completed within five minutes
comparator.quote: Dr Sarpong noted that currently, the assessment and classification of goods involved considerable human effort, which could take up to two hours after importers submitted their documentation. With the introduction of the AI tool, he said, assessments could be completed within five minutes, thereby improving speed and efficiency in clearance processes.

later.note: After full implementation from April 2026, GRA said customs collections rose from about GH¢4 billion a month to GH¢6.1 billion in July 2026.
later.quote: Commissioner-General of the GRA, Anthony Sarpong, said monthly customs revenue averaged about GH¢4 billion before the full implementation of the system, indicating an increase of about GH¢2.1 billion in July.

value.quote: The system has already enabled the government to recover GH¢15 million from fraudulent importers and aims to address significant revenue leakages in Ghana's customs operations.
